operating_notes.text: Total business reached ₹4.88 lakh Cr as of 31 December 2024, up 12.18% YoY and 2.95% QoQ.
Credit-deposit ratio increased to 74.55% as of 31 December 2024 from 71.77% as of 30 September 2024.
CARE Ratings upgraded Tier II Bond rating to AA/Stable from AA-/Positive.
Non-Performing Loan Provisioning Coverage Ratio stood at 97.79% as on 31 March 2026.
Bank holds forward looking provision of ₹1,037.59 Cr on account of Expected Credit Loss (ECL).
Total business reached ₹5.85 lakh Cr as of 31 March 2026 (Deposits ₹3.28 lakh Cr, Advances ₹2.58 lakh Cr).
GST appellate order dated 24.04.2026 substantially allowed UCO Bank's appeal, reducing the CGST Mumbai demand from ₹1,473.48 Cr to ₹4.86 Cr plus interest and penalty.
ECLGS sanctions stood at ₹2,150 Cr and disbursements at ₹1,700 Cr as of yesterday [July 22, 2026]
SMA book (1 crore and above) improved to ₹1,009 Cr (0.36% of advances) from ₹1,125 Cr (0.43% of advances) in March 2026
Digital business balance sheet grew to ₹35,000 Cr as of 30 June 2026 from ₹25,000 Cr as of 31 March 2026
Board approved raising foreign currency funds up to USD 1.00 Billion via Debt Instruments under an MTN Programme.
UFBU issued strike notices for 11 Sep, 28-30 Sep, and continuous from 26 Oct 2026 across PSU banks.
Domestic advances stood at ₹2.57 lakh Cr (+25.98% YoY) and domestic deposits reached ₹3.32 lakh Cr (+14.48% YoY) in Q2FY27.
India Ratings reaffirmed Long-term Issuer and Basel III Tier II bond ratings at AA/Stable on ₹1,500 Cr bonds.
Provisioning Coverage Ratio stood at 98.36% as on 30 September 2026.
Bank transitioned to lower tax regime under Section 115BAA from FY 2026-27.
Recovery in written-off accounts contributed ₹301.16 Cr to other income in Q2FY27.
Global advances reached ₹2,87,690 crore, up 24.70% year-on-year.

timeline.summary: Reported Q3FY25 provisional business update with total advances up 16.2% YoY to ₹2.08 lakh Cr and total deposits up 9.37% YoY to ₹2.80 lakh Cr.
CARE Ratings upgraded UCO Bank's Tier II Bond rating to 'AA/Stable' from 'AA-/Positive'.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): interest earned ₹6,656.33 Cr, net profit ₹801.15 Cr (+22.8% YoY).
UCO Bank’s **Vikash Gupta** (Finance Department) uploaded the recording of the Post Earnings Call with Analysts held on 27.04.2026 via the bank’s website.
UCO Bank reported Q4FY26 net profit of ₹801 Cr (+22% YoY) with gross NPA improving to 2.17%.
GST appellate authority largely allowed UCO Bank's appeal on 24 April 2026, cutting a CGST Mumbai demand from ₹1,473.48 Cr to ₹4.86 Cr plus interest and penalty.
UCO Bank's MD & CEO Shri Ashwani Kumar ceased office on 31 May 2026 on completion of his three-year tenure, with no successor named in the filing.
Q1FY27 results (standalone): interest earned ₹6,996 Cr (+8.7% YoY), net profit ₹656.33 Cr (+8.0% YoY).
Fitch Ratings assigned first-time BBB- IDR with Stable Outlook to UCO Bank on 27 July 2026
UCO Bank reported Q1FY27 results with operating profit up 79.8% YoY to ₹2,810 Cr and net profit up 8% YoY to ₹656 Cr, impacted by a one-time DTA charge from the shift to the new tax regime.
Board approved raising foreign currency funds up to USD 1.00 billion via a Medium Term Note (MTN) Programme.
Received notice from UFBU for proposed nationwide bank strikes in September and continuous strike from October 26, 2026.
Q2FY27 provisional business: total advances up 24.68% YoY to ₹2.88 lakh Cr and deposits up 14.05% YoY to ₹3.49 lakh Cr.
India Ratings reaffirmed UCO Bank's Long-term Issuer and Basel III Tier II Bond ratings at AA/Stable on ₹1,500 Cr bonds on 9 October 2026.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): interest earned ₹7,286.32 Cr (+11.5% YoY), net profit ₹785.64 Cr (+26.8% YoY).
UCO Bank hosted its Q2FY27 post-earnings analyst call reporting 24.7% YoY growth in global advances and a net profit of ₹786 Cr.

watchlist.response: Had not been there, then it could have been added into the profit. So simply saying we could have more profits and then we can calculate the ROA, that could have been more than 1% also. That is our rough estimate, but we have not calculated by that way, because ultimately, this is the situation and this is the final number, which we have.
watchlist.text: What would have been our ROA had we remained in the older tax regime?

watchlist.response: So in the banking space, we know that for competition, there are many players in the financial markets. So public sector banks are there, private sector banks are there, then in some pockets like rural and other pockets, some RRBs are also there, then NBFCs are also nowadays providing credit support to people. So means financial market is full of all these various types of players. So we don't see this as a competition only, we see this as an opportunity also.
watchlist.text: Where are we getting the competition from? From the public sector bank only or from the private sector or NBFCs?

watchlist.response: As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector. As of now, we have not seen any such risk. No stress we have seen.
watchlist.text: Which are the areas… you talked about some areas in the previous question, where we are getting the maximum growth from? And where do we see risk? In which customer segment we see the risk coming from?
